stops.date_confidence: the letter was written in the first months of 1897; no start date is recorded and month and day are defaulted to 01. Roughly 50,000 words. Ross published an abridgement in 1905 under a title Wilde never used; a fuller 1949 edition by Vyvyan Holland was still full of transcription errors, and the first accurate complete text appeared only in Rupert Hart-Davis's 1962 edition of the letters, taken from the manuscript held under a fifty-year access restriction Ross himself imposed.

stops.segment: The Old Bailey and Reading Gaol
stops.stop: Pentonville: out on the morning of the nineteenth
stops.date_confidence: the release date and the mechanism are both corrected. Wikipedia states 'Wilde was released from prison on 19 May 1897'; he was moved from Reading to Pentonville on the evening of 18 May and released from Pentonville the following morning, so he was not released from Reading Gaol at all, and he crossed to France the same night rather than the next day. Wikipedia's own summary line, 'incarcerated from 25 May 1895 to 18 May 1897', is internally inconsistent with its explicit release sentence; the 19 May date is the one used here.

The conditional baptism by Father Cuthbert Dunne on 29 November is tagged [R]: it is reported by Dunne and by Robert Ross and is not corroborated by a third witness, and the degree of conscious assent is disputed. The wallpaper epigram is legend; Quote Investigator finds no bedside witness recording it as his last words, and it most likely began as an earlier joke about the room and was recast afterwards.

stops.stop: Pere Lachaise: the Epstein monument covered and uncovered
stops.date_confidence: the installation year is corrected. Crowell (branchcollective.org) gives a commission announced at a Ritz dinner in December 1908, two thousand pounds from an anonymous donor later revealed as Helen Carew, the sculpture arriving in Paris in August 1912 and being covered and put under guard at once, and the unveiling only in August 1914 after two years of suppression. The pool gave 1912 as the unveiling. The compromise object fixed over the figure is described by Wikipedia as a bronze butterfly-shaped plaque rather than the plaster the pool named. The chiselling off of the genitals is dated 1961. The day here is defaulted to 01.

stops.stop: Merrion Square: the figure on the quartz boulder
stops.date_confidence: the unveiling is dated 1997 without a month or day; both are defaulted to 01. Danny Osborne's three-part sculpture was commissioned by the Guinness Ireland Group and unveiled by Merlin Holland (Wikipedia, Oscar Wilde Memorial Sculpture). The coordinate is the memorial's own point in the north-west corner of the square, opposite No. 1. A second memorial, Maggi Hambling's 'A Conversation with Oscar Wilde', was unveiled on Adelaide Street, London, on 30 November 1998, the anniversary of his death; it is not given a stop here because Wilde had no recorded connection to that street.
